problem.title: Design a Multi-Tenant Enterprise Skill-Based Agent Platform

spark.summary: Design a multi-tenant enterprise agent platform hosting 1,000+ versioned skills across 500 organizations with <50ms skill routing, zero-trust RBAC/secret isolation, and immutable compliance auditing.
spark.keyTakeaway: If model quality drifts from offline training baselines, pair a versioned, CI-scanned Skill Registry with an RBAC-filtered semantic router, lazy-load context hydrator, per-tenant secret vault, and isolated MCP execution workers.
spark.byteSummary:
Scaling a skill-based agent platform to 500 enterprise tenants and 1,000+ org-specific and global skills introduces strict multi-tenancy, latency, and compliance challenges. Each organization customizes workflows (`SKILL.md`), connects private internal APIs via MCP, and demands cryptographic proof that Tenant A's skills or secrets never leak to Tenant B.

The platform divides into four layers: (1) a Versioned Skill Registry & CI Security Scanner storing signed bundles in S3/Postgres; (2) a Semantic Skill Router & Lazy-Load Context Hydrator selecting top-K permitted skills in <50ms; (3) a Per-Tenant Policy & Secret Vault issuing short-lived delegated OAuth tokens; and (4) Isolated Tool Execution Workers running bundled scripts and MCP calls with an immutable Kafka -> S3/ClickHouse audit log.

Key trade-offs include pre-filtering vector search by `(tenant_id, role_set)` to prevent forbidden skill leakage, and caching hydrated skill bundles in regional Redis with digest-keyed invalidation.

learningJourney.title: Multi-Tenant Skill Registry & Digest Versioning
learningJourney.purpose: Store global platform skills and tenant-private overrides with instant rollback.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Multi-Tenant Skill Registry & Digest Versioning** as the intuition layer for Design a Multi-Tenant Enterprise Skill-Based Agent Platform: Store global platform skills and tenant-private overrides with instant rollback.
explanation.core: PostgreSQL stores skill metadata (`tenant_id`, `skill_name`, `semver`, `sha256_digest`, `status`), while immutable skill tarballs (`SKILL.md`, `scripts/`, `assets/`) live in S3 keyed by `sha256_digest`. Tenants inherit global skills and override specific names via `(tenant_id, skill_name)` precedence, allowing instant zero-downtime rollbacks by flipping the active pointer.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, multi-tenant skill registry & digest versioning becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Enforce CI AST/prompt-injection admission, gVisor/Firecracker script isolation, PrivateLink connectors, and WORM audit logs.

learningJourney.title: CI Security Scanner & Supply-Chain Admission
learningJourney.purpose: Automatically vet every tenant-uploaded skill before it can execute in production.

explanation.foundation: Think of **CI Security Scanner & Supply-Chain Admission** as the intuition layer for Design a Multi-Tenant Enterprise Skill-Based Agent Platform: Automatically vet every tenant-uploaded skill before it can execute in production.
explanation.core: Before a skill version transitions from `DRAFT` to `ACTIVE`, an async CI pipeline runs Semgrep/Bandit AST scans on bundled scripts (blocking `subprocess`, raw sockets, `eval`), checks `SKILL.md` with a prompt-injection classifier, and verifies declared MCP scopes against the tenant's allowed connector list.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, ci security scanner & supply-chain admission becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Enforce CI AST/prompt-injection admission, gVisor/Firecracker script isolation, PrivateLink connectors, and WORM audit logs.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design a Multi-Tenant Enterprise Skill-Based Agent Platform without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: If model quality drifts from offline training baselines, pair a versioned, CI-scanned Skill Registry with an RBAC-filtered semantic router, lazy-load context hydrator, per-tenant secret vault, and isolated MCP execution workers.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When Design a Multi-Tenant Enterprise Skill-Based Agent Platform experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

learningJourney.title: RBAC-Filtered Semantic Skill Router (<50ms)
learningJourney.purpose: Retrieve the top-K relevant and authorized skills from 1,000+ candidates in milliseconds.

explanation.foundation: Think of **RBAC-Filtered Semantic Skill Router (<50ms)** as the intuition layer for Design a Multi-Tenant Enterprise Skill-Based Agent Platform: Retrieve the top-K relevant and authorized skills from 1,000+ candidates in milliseconds.
explanation.core: Each skill's description is embedded into a 384-dim vector stored in Qdrant/pgvector with payload attributes `(tenant_id, allowed_groups)`. At query time, the router embeds the user's intent (~5ms) and runs a filtered ANN search (`tenant_id IN ('global', caller_tenant) AND allowed_groups && caller_groups`), returning the top-10 permitted skills to the agent.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, rbac-filtered semantic skill router (<50ms) becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Enforce CI AST/prompt-injection admission, gVisor/Firecracker script isolation, PrivateLink connectors, and WORM audit logs.

learningJourney.title: Lazy-Load Context Hydrator & Token-Budget Guard
learningJourney.purpose: Inject only needed SKILL.md sections and assets without blowing the model's context window.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Lazy-Load Context Hydrator & Token-Budget Guard** as the intuition layer for Design a Multi-Tenant Enterprise Skill-Based Agent Platform: Inject only needed SKILL.md sections and assets without blowing the model's context window.
explanation.core: When the agent calls `lookup_skills(['incident-triage'])`, the Context Hydrator fetches the bundle from Redis, verifies its SHA-256 signature, enforces a per-skill token ceiling (e.g., max 4K tokens for `SKILL.md`), and tracks hydrated skills in session state so repeat calls in the same conversation return a lightweight reference rather than duplicating text.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, lazy-load context hydrator & token-budget guard becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Enforce CI AST/prompt-injection admission, gVisor/Firecracker script isolation, PrivateLink connectors, and WORM audit logs.

learningJourney.title: Per-Tenant Policy & Secret Vault (Delegated OAuth)
learningJourney.purpose: Authenticate MCP tool calls across 500 enterprises without storing long-lived god keys.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Per-Tenant Policy & Secret Vault (Delegated OAuth)** as the intuition layer for Design a Multi-Tenant Enterprise Skill-Based Agent Platform: Authenticate MCP tool calls across 500 enterprises without storing long-lived god keys.
explanation.core: The Per-Tenant Secret Vault (HashiCorp Vault / KMS) stores tenant OAuth app credentials and per-user encrypted refresh tokens. When an execution worker runs an MCP tool, the Vault mints a short-lived (60s), scope-narrowed access token for that specific user and connector, ensuring Salesforce/Jira audit logs record the exact human principal.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, per-tenant policy & secret vault (delegated oauth) becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Enforce CI AST/prompt-injection admission, gVisor/Firecracker script isolation, PrivateLink connectors, and WORM audit logs.

learningJourney.title: Isolated Tool Execution Workers & MCP Connection Pooling
learningJourney.purpose: Execute bundled skill scripts and high-throughput MCP calls safely per tenant.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Isolated Tool Execution Workers & MCP Connection Pooling** as the intuition layer for Design a Multi-Tenant Enterprise Skill-Based Agent Platform: Execute bundled skill scripts and high-throughput MCP calls safely per tenant.
explanation.core: Bundled skill scripts run inside tenant-tagged gVisor/Firecracker sandboxes with read-only skill mounts and zero cross-tenant network reachability. Meanwhile, stateless MCP Proxy Workers maintain TLS connection pools to enterprise SaaS endpoints with per-tenant circuit breakers so a slow Tenant A Jira instance never stalls Tenant B.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, isolated tool execution workers & mcp connection pooling becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Enforce CI AST/prompt-injection admission, gVisor/Firecracker script isolation, PrivateLink connectors, and WORM audit logs.

learningJourney.title: Immutable Compliance Audit Log & Tenant FinOps
learningJourney.purpose: Deliver SOC2/HIPAA-grade immutable audit trails and per-skill cost attribution.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Immutable Compliance Audit Log & Tenant FinOps** as the intuition layer for Design a Multi-Tenant Enterprise Skill-Based Agent Platform: Deliver SOC2/HIPAA-grade immutable audit trails and per-skill cost attribution.
explanation.core: Every skill load, policy decision, and MCP tool invocation writes a hash-chained `AuditEvent` (`tenant_id`, `user_id`, `skill_digest`, `tool_name`, `redacted_args`, `outcome`) to Kafka -> S3 Object Lock (WORM) + ClickHouse. Tenants query real-time dashboards for adoption, failure hotspots, and token spend per department.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, immutable compliance audit log & tenant finops becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Enforce CI AST/prompt-injection admission, gVisor/Firecracker script isolation, PrivateLink connectors, and WORM audit logs.

knowledgeChecks.question: When retrieving candidate skills from a 1,000-skill vector index across 500 tenants, why must RBAC and tenant filtering happen inside the vector query (pre-filtering) rather than after?

options.text: Post-filtering can return 0 valid results if the top-K matches belong to other tenants, and risks leaking forbidden skill names.
options.feedback: Correct! Pre-filtering guarantees both recall (top-K permitted skills) and strict tenant/RBAC isolation.

options.text: Vector databases cannot store string metadata.
options.feedback: Modern vector DBs (Qdrant, pgvector) natively support payload filtering.

options.text: Pre-filtering removes the need for an OIDC token.
options.feedback: The caller's OIDC claims provide the filter predicate.

options.text: Post-filtering is only supported in Python.
options.feedback: Filtering is a database query capability, independent of client language.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Pre-filtering by `(tenant_id, allowed_groups)` ensures all K returned candidates are authorized for the caller, preventing both empty result sets and data leaks.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should the Skill Registry key cached skill bundles in Redis and S3 by `sha256_digest` rather than `(tenant_id, skill_name, 'latest')`?

options.text: Content-addressed digests are immutable, eliminating stale-cache race conditions and enabling instant pointer-flip rollbacks.
options.feedback: Correct! Immutable digest keys never serve stale versions and make rollbacks atomic.

options.text: Because S3 does not support filenames with letters.
options.feedback: S3 supports arbitrary string keys; SHA-256 is used for immutability.

options.text: To allow tenants to read each other's private skills.
options.feedback: Tenant isolation is enforced by the registry metadata lookup.
Digests are signed only after CI scanning passes.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Content-addressing by SHA-256 prevents cache-coherency bugs during skill updates and lets rollbacks happen instantaneously by updating a Postgres pointer.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does the platform prevent a slow or rate-limited Jira instance belonging to Tenant A from degrading agent tool execution for Tenant B?

options.text: By disabling retries for all tenants.
options.feedback: Disabling retries hurts reliability for healthy tenants.

options.text: By using bulkhead isolation: per-tenant worker queues and per-tenant circuit breakers in the MCP Proxy Pool.
options.feedback: Correct! Per-tenant bulkheads and circuit breakers contain noisy-neighbor upstream stalls.

options.text: By sharing a single global connection pool with no timeouts.
options.feedback: A shared unbounded pool would let Tenant A exhaust all connections.

options.text: By running all tenants inside a single shared gVisor sandbox.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Per-tenant bulkheads and circuit breakers ensure upstream latency or 429s in one enterprise tenant never starve worker capacity for others.

beginner.summary: Design a multi-tenant enterprise agent platform where 500 companies safely run 1,000+ custom AI skills.
beginner.keyTakeaway: If model quality drifts from offline training baselines, pair a versioned, CI-scanned Skill Registry with an RBAC-filtered semantic router, lazy-load context hydrator, per-tenant secret vault, and isolated MCP execution workers.
beginner.byteSummary:
In a multi-tenant enterprise platform, hundreds of companies share the same core AI infrastructure while keeping their custom workflows and API keys strictly private.

A fast router finds only the skills a user is allowed to use, a secret vault issues short-lived tokens for tools like Jira or Salesforce, and isolated workers keep every company's data safe.

intermediate.summary: Architect a content-addressed Skill Registry, RBAC-filtered vector router, delegated OAuth vault, and bulkhead MCP pools.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: If model quality drifts from offline training baselines, pair a versioned, CI-scanned Skill Registry with an RBAC-filtered semantic router, lazy-load context hydrator, per-tenant secret vault, and isolated MCP execution workers.
intermediate.byteSummary:
The platform stores immutable, SHA-256-addressed skill bundles in S3 and regional Redis, with Postgres pointers enabling instant rollbacks. An RBAC-pre-filtered vector router selects top-10 permitted skills in <50ms, and a deduplicating Context Hydrator enforces token ceilings.

A Per-Tenant Secret Vault mints 60-second delegated OAuth tokens for bulkhead-isolated MCP Proxy Workers.

advanced.summary: Enforce CI AST/prompt-injection admission, gVisor/Firecracker script isolation, PrivateLink connectors, and WORM audit logs.
advanced.keyTakeaway: If model quality drifts from offline training baselines, pair a versioned, CI-scanned Skill Registry with an RBAC-filtered semantic router, lazy-load context hydrator, per-tenant secret vault, and isolated MCP execution workers.
advanced.byteSummary:
Every skill bundle passes Semgrep AST scans and prompt-injection classifiers before Cosign signing. Bundled scripts run in tenant-tagged gVisor/Firecracker sandboxes, while internal connectors support mTLS and AWS PrivateLink.

All policy and tool events stream into Kafka, archiving hash-chained records to S3 Object Lock (WORM) for 7-year compliance and ClickHouse for departmental ROI.
